learn.hook: A toy car moves, a cloud grows bigger, a candle 'breathes' air to burn. Are they alive? Let's find the real test!
points: Living things need food, water and air to live.
Living things breathe (take in air) and get energy from food. This is called respiration.
Living things grow, respond to changes around them (stimuli), get rid of wastes (excretion) and reproduce (make young ones of their own kind).
Most animals move from place to place; plants show movement too, like a chhui-mui (touch-me-not) folding its leaves when touched.
Living things have a life span: they are born, grow, grow old and die. Non-living things may show one or two of these features, but never all of them.

example.q: A car moves and uses fuel. Is it a living thing?
steps: A car moves and uses fuel, so it shows some features.
But it does not grow, breathe, reproduce or respond to touch on its own.
A living thing must show all the features of life.
example.answer: No. A car is non-living; it shows only a few features, not all.

learn.reallife: When you water a wilting tulsi plant and it perks up, or a puppy runs to you when called, you are seeing living things respond.

games.title: Feature of life
pairs: breathing and getting energy from food
making young ones of its own kind
reacting to changes like touch or light

quiz.q: Which feature is shown by ALL living things?
quiz.explain: Every living thing needs food for energy: plants make their own, animals eat it. Legs, wings and leaves are found only in some.
quiz.mistake: Picks a feature found in only some living things

quiz.q: A chhui-mui (touch-me-not) folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants:
quiz.explain: Folding leaves after a touch is a response to a stimulus.
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants cannot respond

quiz.q: Why is a cloud NOT a living thing, even though it grows bigger?
options: It does not breathe, eat or reproduce
quiz.explain: Growing alone is not enough. A cloud does not show the other features of life.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one feature is enough to be living

quiz.q: What is respiration?
options: Breathing and getting energy from food
quiz.explain: In respiration, living things use air to release energy from food.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up respiration with other life processes

quiz.q: Getting rid of wastes from the body is called:
quiz.explain: Excretion removes harmful waste materials from the body.
quiz.mistake: Confuses excretion with other features

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-living thing?
quiz.explain: A bicycle can be moved, but it does not breathe, grow or reproduce.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mushrooms are non-living

quiz.q: Living things have a life span. This means they:
options: Are born, grow, grow old and die
quiz.explain: Every living thing goes through stages and finally dies.
quiz.mistake: Thinks living things never die

quiz.q: Do plants need air?
quiz.explain: All living things, including plants, need air for respiration.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only animals breathe

teach.ask: Gappu points at a moving car and a sleeping cat: 'The car moves and the cat is still. So is the car alive and the cat not?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Moving is not enough. The cat eats, breathes, grows, responds and has kittens. The car does none of that!
teach.nudge: What features must a living thing show? Does the car grow or have babies?

topics.title: Seeds and plants are alive too

learn.hook: A tiny dry moong seed looks lifeless. Add water, and in two days it sprouts! Was it alive all along?
points: A seed is a living thing that is resting. When conditions are right, it wakes up and starts to grow. This is called germination.
Seeds need water, air and a suitable (warm, not too cold) temperature to germinate.
Seeds kept dry do not germinate. Seeds kept fully under water (without air) usually do not germinate either. Seeds kept in a fridge germinate poorly or not at all.
Most seeds like moong and chana can germinate even in the dark.
Plants grow, take in air through tiny pores in their leaves, make their own food in sunlight, respond (roots grow towards water, shoots towards light) and make seeds.

example.q: Arnav sets up three cups of moong seeds: A dry, B on wet cotton, C fully under water. Which sprout well and why?
steps: Cup A has air and warmth but no water: no sprouting.
Cup B has water, air and warmth: good sprouting.
Cup C has water but very little air: little or no sprouting.
example.answer: Only cup B sprouts well, because seeds need water, air and suitable warmth.

learn.reallife: Moong and chana sprouts are a healthy breakfast in many Indian homes. Soaking and keeping them in a damp cloth gives them water, air and warmth to germinate.

games.title: Seed science
items: A seed is a living thing.
It is resting; given the right conditions it germinates and grows.
Seeds kept fully under water always sprout best.
Seeds under water get very little air, so they usually do not germinate.
Seeds germinate best in a fridge.
Too cold a temperature stops or slows germination.
Moong seeds can sprout in the dark.
Light is not needed for moong seeds to germinate.
The shoot of a plant grows towards light.
Plants respond to light by growing towards it.

items.text: The sprouting of a seed is called ___.
Seeds need water, air and suitable ___ to germinate.
The roots of a plant grow towards ___.
Plants take in air through tiny ___ in their leaves.

quiz.q: What is germination?
options: A seed starting to sprout and grow
quiz.explain: Germination is when a resting seed wakes up and begins to grow.
quiz.mistake: Confuses germination with other plant changes

quiz.q: Which conditions do seeds need to germinate?
options: Water, air and a suitable temperature
quiz.explain: Seeds need water, air and suitable warmth. Many sprout even without soil or light.
quiz.mistake: Thinks soil or light is the main need

quiz.q: Why do seeds kept fully under water usually not germinate?
quiz.explain: Seeds need air too. Under water, they get very little air.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more water is always better

quiz.q: Seeds were kept on wet cotton in a fridge. They did not sprout. Why?
options: They had no air at all
quiz.explain: They had water and air, but the cold temperature stopped germination.
quiz.mistake: Does not consider temperature as a need

quiz.q: Is a dry seed living or non-living?
quiz.explain: A dry seed is alive but resting. With the right conditions it germinates.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a seed is non-living because it does not move

quiz.q: Which shows that plants respond to their surroundings?
quiz.explain: Bending towards light is a response to a stimulus.
quiz.mistake: Picks a feature that is not a response

quiz.q: Plants take in air through:
options: Nothing; plants do not need air
quiz.explain: Leaves have tiny pores through which air goes in and out.
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants do not breathe

quiz.q: Riya wants moong sprouts for breakfast. What should she do?
options: Soak the seeds and keep them in a damp cloth
Keep them dry in a tin
quiz.explain: Soaking gives water, and a damp cloth keeps air and warmth, so they germinate.
quiz.mistake: Does not apply the conditions for germination

teach.ask: Gappu holds a dry seed: 'This looks like a tiny pebble. How can it be alive? And what does it need to grow?'
teach.praise: Chirp! A seed is alive but resting. Give it water, air and warmth, and it germinates!
teach.nudge: Is the seed living? And what three things does it need to sprout?

learn.hook: A frog was once a tiny tadpole with a tail, and a butterfly was once a crawling caterpillar. Life is full of surprises!
points: A life cycle is the series of stages a living thing goes through from birth to becoming an adult that can produce young ones.
Frog: egg → tadpole (lives in water, has a tail, breathes with gills) → froglet (grows legs) → adult frog.
Mosquito: egg → larva → pupa → adult. The eggs, larvae and pupae live in still (stagnant) water, so we must not let water collect in coolers, pots or tyres.
Butterfly: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa (also called a chrysalis) → adult butterfly. Big changes in body shape like these are called metamorphosis.
Plant: seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds → new plants.

example.q: Why do health workers ask people to empty water from coolers and old tyres every week, especially in the rainy season?
steps: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water.
The larvae and pupae also grow in that water before becoming adults.
Emptying the water breaks the life cycle, so fewer mosquitoes are born.
example.answer: To stop mosquitoes from breeding, by removing the still water their eggs, larvae and pupae need.

learn.reallife: During the monsoon you may see tadpoles in puddles and ponds. Silk is made from the cocoons that silkworms spin when they become pupae; they later turn into moths.

games.title: Which life cycle has this stage?

quiz.q: Which is the correct life cycle of a frog?
quiz.explain: A frog hatches from an egg as a tadpole, grows legs as a froglet, then becomes an adult.
quiz.mistake: Uses the insect life cycle stages for a frog

quiz.q: Where do mosquitoes lay their eggs?
quiz.explain: Mosquito eggs, larvae and pupae all develop in still water.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where mosquitoes breed

quiz.q: What is the larva of a butterfly called?
quiz.explain: The butterfly larva is a caterpillar that eats leaves and grows.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the young stages of different animals

quiz.q: How does a tadpole breathe?
options: It does not need to breathe
quiz.explain: Tadpoles live in water and breathe using gills.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a tadpole breathes like an adult frog

quiz.q: Which stage comes just before the adult in a mosquito's life cycle?
quiz.explain: The order is egg → larva → pupa → adult.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of larva and pupa

quiz.q: What is metamorphosis?
options: A big change in body shape during the life cycle
quiz.explain: A caterpillar turning into a butterfly or a tadpole into a frog is metamorphosis.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the term

quiz.q: Which is the correct life cycle of a plant?
options: Seed → seedling → adult plant → flowers → fruits with seeds
quiz.explain: A seed germinates into a seedling, grows into an adult plant, flowers, and makes fruits with seeds.
quiz.mistake: Gets the order of plant stages wrong

quiz.q: How does emptying water from a cooler every week help?
quiz.explain: Removing still water breaks the mosquito life cycle before larvae become adults.
quiz.mistake: Does not link stagnant water with mosquito breeding

teach.ask: Gappu sees tadpoles in a pond: 'Mama Frog says these wiggly things are her babies! But they don't look like frogs at all. How?'
teach.praise: Ribbit-tweet! Egg, tadpole, froglet, frog. The babies change shape as they grow: that's a life cycle with metamorphosis!
teach.nudge: What stage comes after the egg? And what changes before it becomes a frog?
